shorts.title: Osiris and Set: The Brother Who Sealed a King in a Box
shorts.covers: Set tricks Osiris into a beautiful chest, seals it and throws it into the Nile, and Isis searches the world to bring her husband back.
shorts.source: Plutarch, On Isis and Osiris (Babbitt translation, Loeb 1936)

script.title: Osiris and Set: The King in the Box
script.description: A jealous brother builds a beautiful chest, shaped to fit one man exactly. Then he invites the king of Egypt to a feast, and offers it as a prize to whoever fits inside.

shorts.title: Gilgamesh and Enkidu: The King Who Met His Match
shorts.covers: The gods make a wild man to tame a tyrant king, the two fight in the street, and become friends who kill the guardian of the cedar forest.
shorts.source: The Epic of Gilgamesh (R. Campbell Thompson translation, 1928), tablets 1 to 5

script.title: Gilgamesh and Enkidu: King Meets His Match
script.description: The gods made a wild man from clay to stop a cruel king. The two met in a doorway, fought until the walls shook, and became the most famous friends in the world's oldest story.

shorts.title: Cú Chulainn: How a Boy Became the Hound of Culann
shorts.covers: A small boy kills a smith's ferocious guard dog with a ball and stick, offers to guard the house himself, and takes the name he will be known by forever.
shorts.source: Lady Gregory, Cuchulain of Muirthemne (1902), the boy deeds of Cuchulain

script.title: Cú Chulainn: The Boy and the Hound
script.description: A small boy arrives late at a feast, and the guard dog is already loose in the dark. What he does next gives him the name Ireland's greatest hero is known by forever.

shorts.title: Izanagi and Izanami: The Gods Who Made Japan
shorts.covers: Two gods stir the ocean with a spear to make the islands, and after Izanami dies, Izanagi follows her into the land of the dead.
shorts.source: The Kojiki (Basil Hall Chamberlain translation, 1882), sections 1 to 10

script.title: Izanagi and Izanami: The Gods Who Made Japan
script.description: Two gods stir the ocean with a spear and build the islands of Japan together. Then one of them dies, and the other follows her into the land of the dead, against every warning.

shorts.title: Pangu: The Giant Who Pushed the Sky Away
shorts.covers: A giant hatches from a cosmic egg, holds heaven and earth apart for eighteen thousand years, and his body becomes the world.
shorts.source: E. T. C. Werner, Myths and Legends of China (1922), the creation of the world

script.title: Pangu: The Giant Who Pushed the Sky Away
script.description: Before anything existed, there was a cosmic egg, and inside it a giant was growing. When he finally broke out, he spent eighteen thousand years holding the sky away from the earth.

shorts.title: Vasilisa and Baba Yaga
shorts.covers: A girl is sent to fetch fire from the witch in the hut on chicken legs, carrying only a tiny doll her mother left her.
shorts.source: Vasilisa the Beautiful, in Post Wheeler, Russian Wonder Tales (1912)

script.title: Vasilisa and Baba Yaga
script.description: A girl is sent into the dark forest to fetch fire from the most feared witch in Russia. All she carries is a tiny doll her dying mother gave her, with a secret.

shorts.title: The Fifth Sun: The God Who Leapt Into the Fire
shorts.covers: The gods gather in darkness to make a new sun, the proud one hesitates, and a small sickly god jumps into the flames first.
shorts.source: Lewis Spence, The Myths of Mexico and Peru (1913), and Sahagún's account of Teotihuacan

script.title: The Fifth Sun: The God Who Leapt Into Fire
script.description: The world was dark, and the Aztec gods needed one of them to become the new sun. A proud god said he would do it. Then a small, sick, forgotten god stepped forward too.

shorts.title: Anansi: The Spider Who Bought the Sky God's Stories
shorts.covers: Anansi asks the sky god for all the world's stories, and must capture a python, a leopard, hornets and a fairy to pay for them.
shorts.source: R. S. Rattray, Akan-Ashanti Folk-Tales (1930), how the sky god's stories came to be Anansi's

script.title: Anansi: The Spider Who Bought the Stories
script.description: Anansi the spider wants to own every story in the world, so he asks the sky god for them. The price is four impossible captures: a python, a leopard, a swarm of hornets and a fairy.

shorts.title: The Sword in the Stone
shorts.covers: A sword is set in a stone with a promise that whoever pulls it out is the rightful king, and a young squire does it without trying.
shorts.source: Thomas Malory, Le Morte d'Arthur (1485), book 1

script.title: The Sword in the Stone
script.description: A sword appears in a stone in a London churchyard, with words promising the kingdom to whoever can pull it out. The greatest knights in England all fail. Then a teenage squire forgets his brother's sword.

shorts.title: Erysichthon: The King Who Ate Himself
shorts.covers: A king cuts down a sacred oak of the harvest goddess, is cursed with a hunger nothing can fill, sells his own daughter for food, and finally devours his own body.
shorts.source: Ovid, Metamorphoses (Brookes More translation, 1922), book 8

script.title: Erysichthon: The King Who Ate Himself
script.description: A greedy Greek king cuts down a sacred tree that bleeds when the axe hits it. The goddess of the harvest sends him a punishment: a hunger that no amount of food can fill.

shorts.title: Isis and the Secret Name of Ra
shorts.covers: Isis makes a serpent from the old sun god's spit, and Ra, poisoned and in agony, must give up the hidden name that holds his power.
shorts.source: E. A. Wallis Budge, Legends of the Gods (1912), the legend of Ra and Isis

script.title: Isis and the Secret Name of Ra
script.description: The sun god Ra has a secret name that holds all his power. The goddess Isis wants it, so she makes a serpent out of his own spit and lays it on his path.

shorts.title: Gilgamesh and the Plant of Immortality
shorts.covers: Grieving for Enkidu, Gilgamesh crosses the waters of death to find the one man who never died, and loses the plant of youth to a snake.
shorts.source: The Epic of Gilgamesh (R. Campbell Thompson translation, 1928), tablets 9 to 11

script.title: Gilgamesh and the Plant of Youth
script.description: After his best friend dies, King Gilgamesh is terrified of death. He crosses the world and the waters of death to find the one man the gods let live forever.

shorts.title: The Children of Lir: 900 Years as Swans
shorts.covers: A jealous stepmother turns four children into swans, and they spend nine centuries on cold waters until a bell rings out across Ireland.
shorts.source: Lady Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), the fate of the children of Lir

script.title: The Children of Lir: 900 Years as Swans
script.description: A jealous stepmother turns four children into swans with a druid's wand. They keep their human voices, and must spend nine hundred years on Ireland's coldest waters.

shorts.title: Amaterasu: The Sun Goddess Who Hid in a Cave
shorts.covers: Insulted by her storm god brother, the sun goddess shuts herself in a cave and the world goes dark until the gods trick her out.
shorts.source: The Kojiki (Basil Hall Chamberlain translation, 1882), the door of the heavenly rock-dwelling

script.title: Amaterasu: The Sun Goddess in the Cave
script.description: Insulted by her wild storm god brother, the sun goddess of Japan shuts herself in a cave, and the whole world goes dark. Eight hundred gods gather to lure her out.

shorts.title: Nüwa: The Goddess Who Mended the Sky
shorts.covers: Nüwa shapes the first people from yellow clay, and when a pillar of heaven breaks she melts five coloured stones to patch the sky.
shorts.source: The Huainanzi, book 6, and E. T. C. Werner, Myths and Legends of China (1922)

script.title: Nüwa: The Goddess Who Mended the Sky
script.description: A goddess shapes the first people out of yellow mud. Then an angry water god smashes into one of the pillars holding up heaven, and the sky cracks open above them.

shorts.title: Koschei the Deathless: The Sorcerer Who Hid His Death
shorts.covers: A prince's wife is stolen by a sorcerer whose death is hidden in a needle, in an egg, in a duck, in a hare, in an iron chest.
shorts.source: Koschei the Deathless, in W. R. S. Ralston, Russian Folk-Tales (1873)

script.title: Koschei the Deathless: The Hidden Death
script.description: A sorcerer who cannot be killed has stolen a prince's wife. The prince learns why: Koschei has hidden his death far away, in a needle, inside an egg, inside a duck, inside a hare.

shorts.title: Quetzalcoatl: The Feathered Serpent Who Sailed Away
shorts.covers: A wise god-king is tricked by his rival with a mirror and strong drink, shamed, and leaves his people, promising to return.
shorts.source: Lewis Spence, The Myths of Mexico and Peru (1913), the Quetzalcoatl myth

script.title: Quetzalcoatl: The Feathered Serpent's Exile
script.description: A wise and gentle god-king rules a golden city. Then his rival arrives with a mirror and a strong drink, and tricks him into the night that ends his reign.

shorts.title: Anansi and the Pot of Wisdom
shorts.covers: Anansi tries to hide all the wisdom in the world at the top of a tree, and his small son shows him how much he still has to learn.
shorts.source: West African Anansi tales, as collected in R. S. Rattray, Akan-Ashanti Folk-Tales (1930)

script.title: Anansi and the Pot of Wisdom
script.description: Anansi the spider gathers all the wisdom in the world into one pot and tries to hide it at the top of a tree. His small son is watching, and knows something he does not.

shorts.title: Excalibur and the Lady of the Lake
shorts.covers: Arthur breaks his sword in a fight, and Merlin takes him to a lake where a hand rises from the water holding a new one.
shorts.source: Thomas Malory, Le Morte d'Arthur (1485), book 1, chapter 25

script.title: Excalibur and the Lady of the Lake
script.description: King Arthur breaks his sword in a fight he nearly loses. Merlin takes him to a wide lake, and a hand in white silk rises out of the water, holding a new one.

shorts.title: Ceyx and Alcyone: The Couple Who Became Kingfishers
shorts.covers: A king drowns at sea, the god of sleep sends his wife a dream of his death, and the gods turn the grieving pair into birds who calm the winter waves.
shorts.source: Ovid, Metamorphoses (Brookes More translation, 1922), book 11

script.title: Ceyx and Alcyone: The Kingfisher Lovers
script.description: A king sails away against his wife's pleading and is lost in a storm. Every day she prays for his return, until the god of sleep sends her a dream.

shorts.title: Sekhmet: The Goddess Who Was Tricked With Red Beer
shorts.covers: Ra sends his fierce eye to punish rebellious humans, she will not stop killing, and the gods flood the fields with beer dyed red to save humanity.
shorts.source: The Book of the Heavenly Cow, in E. A. Wallis Budge, Legends of the Gods (1912)

script.title: Sekhmet: The Goddess Tricked With Red Beer
script.description: The sun god sends his fiercest daughter to punish humans who plotted against him. She enjoys the killing too much to stop, so the gods flood the fields with beer dyed the colour of blood.

shorts.title: Inanna's Descent to the Underworld
shorts.covers: The queen of heaven goes down to her sister's kingdom of the dead, is stripped at seven gates, killed, and must find someone to take her place.
shorts.source: The Descent of Inanna, in the Electronic Text Corpus of Sumerian Literature (Oxford)

script.title: Inanna's Descent to the Underworld
script.description: The queen of heaven decides to visit her sister, the queen of the dead. At each of seven gates she must give up one of her treasures, and she arrives with nothing.

shorts.title: Fionn and the Salmon of Knowledge
shorts.covers: A poet spends seven years trying to catch a magic salmon, his young servant burns his thumb cooking it, and gains all the wisdom in the world.
shorts.source: Lady Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), the coming of Finn

script.title: Fionn and the Salmon of Knowledge
script.description: An old poet spends seven years trying to catch a magic salmon that holds all the knowledge in the world. When he finally does, he asks his young servant to cook it, and not taste a single bite.

shorts.title: Susanoo and the Eight-Headed Serpent
shorts.covers: The banished storm god meets a family who have lost seven daughters to a monster, and sets a trap with eight bowls of strong sake.
shorts.source: The Kojiki (Basil Hall Chamberlain translation, 1882), the eight-forked serpent

script.title: Susanoo and the Eight-Headed Serpent
script.description: Banished from heaven, the storm god meets an old couple who have lost seven daughters to a monster with eight heads. Their last daughter is next, so he sets a trap with eight bowls of strong rice wine.

shorts.title: Hou Yi: The Archer Who Shot Down Nine Suns
shorts.covers: Ten suns rise at once and scorch the earth, and a great archer shoots nine of them from the sky.
shorts.source: E. T. C. Werner, Myths and Legends of China (1922), the archer and the suns

script.title: Hou Yi: The Archer Who Shot Down Nine Suns
script.description: Ten suns live in a giant tree, and take turns to cross the sky. One morning, all ten rise together, and the earth begins to burn. Only one archer can stop them.

shorts.title: The Firebird
shorts.covers: A prince follows a glowing bird that steals the king's golden apples, helped by a grey wolf on a quest of ever larger thefts.
shorts.source: Prince Ivan, the Firebird and the Grey Wolf, in Post Wheeler, Russian Wonder Tales (1912)

script.title: The Firebird
script.description: A blazing bird is stealing the golden apples from the tsar's garden. His youngest son grabs one feather, and sets off on a quest with the help of a grey wolf that eats his horse.

shorts.title: Huitzilopochtli: Born Armed on the Serpent Mountain
shorts.covers: A mother is attacked by her four hundred children, and the war god springs from her womb fully armed to defend her.
shorts.source: Lewis Spence, The Myths of Mexico and Peru (1913), the birth of Huitzilopochtli

script.title: Huitzilopochtli: Born Armed on the Mountain
script.description: A mother goddess becomes pregnant from a ball of feathers. Her four hundred children are so ashamed that they climb the mountain to kill her, just as her last son is born.

shorts.title: Kaggen: The Mantis Who Made the Eland
shorts.covers: The trickster god of the San people secretly raises the first eland from a shoe, and grieves when his family hunt it.
shorts.source: W. H. I. Bleek and L. C. Lloyd, Specimens of Bushman Folklore (1911)

script.title: Kaggen: The Mantis Who Made the Eland
script.description: Kaggen, the trickster god of the San people, secretly raises the first eland from a piece of leather. He loves it like a child, until his family follow him and see what he has been hiding.

shorts.title: Gawain and the Green Knight
shorts.covers: A giant green knight offers a deadly game at Christmas, and Gawain must travel a year later to receive the return blow.
shorts.source: Sir Gawain and the Green Knight (Jessie L. Weston translation, 1898)

script.title: Gawain and the Green Knight
script.description: A giant green knight rides into King Arthur's Christmas feast and offers a deadly game. Gawain cuts off his head, and the knight picks it up and tells him to come and receive the return blow in a year.

shorts.title: King Midas and the Golden Touch
shorts.covers: A king does a kindness for the god of wine and is granted one wish: everything he touches turns to gold. Then he sits down to eat, and cannot eat or drink anything at all.
shorts.source: Ovid, Metamorphoses (Brookes More translation, 1922), book 11

script.title: King Midas and the Golden Touch
script.description: A king does a kindness for a god, and is granted one wish. He asks that everything he touches should turn to gold. Then he sits down to eat.

shorts.title: Horus and Set: The Eighty-Year Trial for the Throne
shorts.covers: The young Horus and his uncle Set fight for Egypt's crown in a long divine court case full of tricks, contests and boats made of stone.
shorts.source: The Contendings of Horus and Set, Chester Beatty Papyrus I, in Alan H. Gardiner's translation

script.title: Horus and Set: The Trial for the Throne
script.description: After the murdered king Osiris goes down to rule the dead, his young son and his brother both claim his crown. The court of the gods argues for eighty years, and the contest gets very strange.

shorts.title: Marduk and Tiamat: The War That Made the World
shorts.covers: The young god Marduk fights the ocean dragon Tiamat, splits her body in two, and builds the sky and earth from the halves.
shorts.source: Enuma Elish, in L. W. King, The Seven Tablets of Creation (1902)

script.title: Marduk and Tiamat: The War That Made Earth
script.description: The goddess of the salt sea raises an army of monsters to destroy the young gods. Only one god dares to face her, and he asks for a price: if he wins, he will be king of them all.

shorts.title: Oisín in Tír na nÓg: The Land of Youth
shorts.covers: A hero rides away with a fairy woman to a land where no one ages, and when he returns home three centuries have passed.
shorts.source: Lady Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Oisin's children and the Land of the Young

script.title: Oisín in Tír na nÓg: The Land of Youth
script.description: A fairy woman on a white horse carries the hero Oisín away over the sea to the Land of Youth. After three happy years he longs to see Ireland again, and she gives him one warning.

shorts.title: The White Hare of Inaba
shorts.covers: A hare who tricked crocodiles is skinned and given cruel advice, until a kind young god shows him how to heal.
shorts.source: The Kojiki (Basil Hall Chamberlain translation, 1882), the white hare of Inaba

script.title: The White Hare of Inaba
script.description: A hare tricks a line of sea monsters into making him a bridge, and pays for it with his fur. Eighty cruel brothers give him terrible advice. Then their youngest brother comes along the beach.

shorts.title: Chang'e: The Woman Who Flew to the Moon
shorts.covers: Hou Yi's wife swallows the elixir of immortality and floats up to the moon, where she lives alone with a jade rabbit.
shorts.source: E. T. C. Werner, Myths and Legends of China (1922), the moon lady

script.title: Chang'e: The Woman Who Flew to the Moon
script.description: The archer Yi is given a potion that can make one person a god. He hides it at home, and his wife Chang'e finds it and drinks it, and begins to float up into the sky.

shorts.title: Sadko in the Palace of the Sea King
shorts.covers: A poor musician of Novgorod wins a fortune by his playing, and is later dragged beneath the waves to play for the king of the sea.
shorts.source: The bylina of Sadko, in Isabel Florence Hapgood, The Epic Songs of Russia (1886)

script.title: Sadko in the Palace of the Sea King
script.description: A poor musician of old Novgorod plays his harp beside a lake, and the King of the Sea rises out of the water to listen. Years later, the king wants him back, under the waves.

shorts.title: Manco Cápac and the Golden Staff
shorts.covers: The sun sends his children to find where a golden staff will sink into the earth, and there they found the city of Cusco.
shorts.source: Garcilaso de la Vega, Royal Commentaries of the Incas (Markham translation, 1869)

script.title: Manco Cápac and the Golden Staff
script.description: The Sun looks down on people living like animals and sends his son and daughter out of a great lake with a golden staff. Wherever it sinks into the ground, they must build a city.

shorts.title: The Chameleon's Message: Why People Die
shorts.covers: The creator sends a slow chameleon with the gift of life and a fast lizard with the message of death, and the lizard arrives first.
shorts.source: Henry Callaway, The Religious System of the Amazulu (1870), the coming of death

script.title: The Chameleon's Message: Why People Die
script.description: The first ancestor of the Zulu people sends a chameleon with a message that people will live forever. But the chameleon is slow, and stops to eat, and a lizard is sent after it with a different message.

shorts.title: Merlin and Nimue: The Wizard Who Was Trapped
shorts.covers: Merlin falls for a young enchantress, teaches her his magic, and she uses it to seal him away forever.
shorts.source: Thomas Malory, Le Morte d'Arthur (1485), book 4

script.title: Merlin and Nimue: The Wizard Who Was Trapped
script.description: Merlin, the greatest wizard in Britain, falls in love with a young enchantress and teaches her all his magic. He has already seen how it ends, and goes with her anyway.

shorts.title: Baucis and Philemon: The Couple Who Fed the Gods
shorts.covers: Two disguised gods are turned away by a whole village except one poor old couple, who are rewarded and the village drowned.
shorts.source: Ovid, Metamorphoses (Brookes More translation, 1922), book 8

script.title: Baucis and Philemon: Supper for the Gods
script.description: Two gods in disguise knock on a thousand doors, and every one is slammed in their faces. Then they come to the smallest hut in the village, where a poor old couple invite them in.

shorts.title: Apep: The Serpent Who Attacks the Sun Every Night
shorts.covers: Each night the sun boat sails through the underworld and the great serpent Apep tries to swallow it, and the gods must fight him off before dawn.
shorts.source: E. A. Wallis Budge, The Gods of the Egyptians (1904), and the Book of Overthrowing Apep

script.title: Apep: The Serpent Who Attacks the Sun
script.description: Every night, the sun god sails his boat through the underworld. And every night, a giant serpent waits in the dark to swallow him, so that morning never comes.

shorts.title: Adapa: The Man Who Refused Eternal Life
shorts.covers: A wise man breaks the wing of the south wind, is called before the sky god, and on his own god's advice turns down the food of immortality.
shorts.source: The Legend of Adapa, in R. W. Rogers, Cuneiform Parallels to the Old Testament (1912)

script.title: Adapa: The Man Who Refused Eternal Life
script.description: A wise man breaks the wing of the south wind, and is summoned to heaven to answer for it. His own god warns him: when the sky god offers you food, do not eat it.

shorts.title: Deirdre of the Sorrows
shorts.covers: A girl is foretold to bring ruin, is raised in hiding for a king, and runs away with the man she loves, with tragic results.
shorts.source: Lady Gregory, Cuchulain of Muirthemne (1902), the fate of the sons of Usnach

script.title: Deirdre of the Sorrows
script.description: Before she is born, a druid foretells that a baby girl will bring ruin to Ulster. The king hides her away to marry her himself, but she falls in love with a young warrior instead.

shorts.title: Urashima Taro: The Fisherman Who Visited the Sea Palace
shorts.covers: A fisherman saves a turtle, is taken to the palace beneath the sea, and returns home with a box he is told never to open.
shorts.source: Yei Theodora Ozaki, Japanese Fairy Tales (1908), the story of Urashima Taro

script.title: Urashima Taro: The Palace Under the Sea
script.description: A young fisherman saves a turtle and is carried down to a palace beneath the sea. When he returns home, a princess gives him a beautiful box, and tells him never to open it.

shorts.title: The Cowherd and the Weaver Girl
shorts.covers: A poor cowherd marries a weaver from heaven, the gods split them with the Milky Way, and they may meet only once a year on a bridge of magpies.
shorts.source: E. T. C. Werner, Myths and Legends of China (1922), the herdsman and the weaving girl

script.title: The Cowherd and the Weaver Girl
script.description: A goddess who weaves the clouds falls in love with a poor cowherd on earth. Heaven drags her home, and draws a river of stars across the sky between them.

shorts.title: Ilya Muromets: The Hero Who Sat Still for Thirty-Three Years
shorts.covers: A peasant who cannot walk is healed by wandering pilgrims, gains great strength, and defeats the monstrous Nightingale the Robber.
shorts.source: Isabel Florence Hapgood, The Epic Songs of Russia (1886), Ilya of Murom

script.title: Ilya Muromets: 33 Years on the Stove
script.description: A peasant boy cannot walk, and sits by the stove until he is thirty-three. Then two strange pilgrims ask him for a drink, and he stands up with the strength of a giant.

shorts.title: Viracocha: The Creator Who Walked Away Over the Sea
shorts.covers: The creator rises from Lake Titicaca, turns his first people to stone, makes the sun and moon, and walks off across the ocean.
shorts.source: Lewis Spence, The Myths of Mexico and Peru (1913), the Viracocha myth

script.title: Viracocha: The Creator Who Walked on the Sea
script.description: The Inca creator rises out of a great lake in the dark. He makes giants from stone, and then the sun and moon and people, and then walks away across the ocean.

shorts.title: Rostam and Sohrab: The Father Who Did Not Know His Son
shorts.covers: Persia's greatest hero fights a young champion from the enemy army, not knowing the boy is his own son.
shorts.source: Ferdowsi, The Shahnameh (A. G. and E. Warner translation, 1905), the tragedy of Sohrab

script.title: Rostam and Sohrab: Father Against Son
script.description: Persia's greatest hero leaves behind an armband for a son he will never meet. Years later, a young champion of the enemy army challenges him, and neither knows who the other is.

shorts.title: The Holy Grail and the Fisher King
shorts.covers: Knights of the Round Table seek the Grail, a wounded king waits in a castle, and only the purest knight can finish the quest.
shorts.source: Thomas Malory, Le Morte d'Arthur (1485), books 13 to 17

script.title: The Holy Grail and the Fisher King
script.description: A sacred cup appears in the air at King Arthur's feast, and the knights swear to find it. Far away, a wounded king waits in a castle, and his land lies dying until someone pure enough arrives.

shorts.title: Phaethon: The Boy Who Drove the Sun
shorts.covers: The son of the sun god begs to drive his father's chariot for one day, loses control and sets the earth on fire.
shorts.source: Ovid, Metamorphoses (Brookes More translation, 1922), books 1 and 2

script.title: Phaethon: The Boy Who Drove the Sun
script.description: A boy is teased that the sun god is not really his father. He travels to the sun's palace to prove it, and asks for one thing: to drive the chariot of the sun for a day.

shorts.title: The Weighing of the Heart
shorts.covers: A dead soul stands in the Hall of Two Truths while its heart is weighed against the feather of Maat, and a monster waits to eat the guilty.
shorts.source: The Egyptian Book of the Dead, Papyrus of Ani (Budge translation, 1895), chapter 125

script.title: The Weighing of the Heart
script.description: An Egyptian scribe called Ani dies and walks into the Hall of Two Truths. His heart is placed on a scale against a single feather, and beside the scale, a monster waits to eat it.

shorts.title: Etana: The King Who Flew on an Eagle
shorts.covers: A childless king rescues an eagle from a pit, and the bird carries him up toward heaven to find the plant of birth.
shorts.source: The Legend of Etana, in R. W. Rogers, Cuneiform Parallels to the Old Testament (1912)

script.title: Etana: The King Who Flew on an Eagle
script.description: A good king has no son to rule after him. A wounded eagle lies trapped at the bottom of a pit, and the sun god tells the king that the eagle can carry him to heaven.

shorts.title: Pwyll: The Prince Who Swapped Places With the King of the Dead
shorts.covers: A Welsh prince offends the lord of the otherworld and agrees to rule his kingdom for a year in his shape.
shorts.source: The Mabinogion (Lady Charlotte Guest translation, 1849), Pwyll Prince of Dyfed

script.title: Pwyll: The Prince Who Swapped With Death
script.description: A Welsh prince insults the king of the otherworld while out hunting. To make up for it, he agrees to swap shapes with him for a whole year, and rule his kingdom of the dead.

shorts.title: Momotaro: The Boy Born From a Peach
shorts.covers: An old couple find a baby inside a giant peach, and he grows up to sail for the island of demons with a dog, a monkey and a pheasant.
shorts.source: Yei Theodora Ozaki, Japanese Fairy Tales (1908), the story of Momotaro

script.title: Momotaro: The Boy Born From a Peach
script.description: An old woman washing clothes in a river sees a giant peach floating towards her. Inside is a baby boy, and when he grows up, he sets off to fight the ogres of Ogre Island.

shorts.title: Sun Wukong: The Monkey Who Wrecked Heaven
shorts.covers: A stone monkey learns magic, eats the peaches of immortality, defeats heaven's armies, and is trapped under a mountain by the Buddha.
shorts.source: Wu Cheng'en, Journey to the West, chapters 1 to 7, in Timothy Richard, A Mission to Heaven (1913)

script.title: Sun Wukong: The Monkey Who Wrecked Heaven
script.description: A monkey born from a stone learns magic, steals the gods' peaches of immortality, and defeats the armies of heaven. Then the Buddha offers him a bet he cannot resist.

shorts.title: Väinämöinen and Joukahainen: The Singing Duel
shorts.covers: A boastful young man challenges the oldest of singers, and is sung into a swamp until he offers his sister in exchange for his life.
shorts.source: The Kalevala (John Martin Crawford translation, 1888), runo 3

script.title: Väinämöinen and the Singing Duel
script.description: A boastful young man challenges the oldest and wisest singer in Finland to a contest of songs. The old man starts to sing, and the young man begins to sink into a swamp.

shorts.title: The People of Maize
shorts.covers: The gods try to make people from mud and then wood, both fail, and the first true humans are made from yellow and white corn.
shorts.source: The Popol Vuh, in Lewis Spence, The Popol Vuh (1908)

script.title: The People of Maize
script.description: The Maya gods try to make people who will speak and remember them. People of mud fall apart. People of wood forget them. Then the animals bring news of yellow and white corn.

shorts.title: Zahhak: The King With Serpents on His Shoulders
shorts.covers: A prince lets a devil kiss his shoulders, snakes grow from them, and they must be fed human brains every day.
shorts.source: Ferdowsi, The Shahnameh (A. G. and E. Warner translation, 1905), Zahhak

script.title: Zahhak: The King With Snakes on His Shoulders
script.description: A prince lets a kindly cook kiss his shoulders as a reward. Two black snakes grow from the spots, and they can only be fed one thing: human brains.

shorts.title: Tristan and Iseult: The Love Potion
shorts.covers: A knight escorts an Irish princess to marry his uncle, they drink a potion by mistake, and fall into a love that destroys them.
shorts.source: Joseph Bédier, The Romance of Tristan and Iseult (Hilaire Belloc translation, 1913)

script.title: Tristan and Iseult: The Love Potion
script.description: A knight sails to Ireland to bring back a bride for his uncle, the king. On the voyage home, on a hot day, he and the princess drink a love potion by mistake.

shorts.title: Pygmalion: The Sculptor Who Fell in Love With His Statue
shorts.covers: A sculptor carves a woman of ivory more beautiful than any living one, and prays to Venus to bring her to life.
shorts.source: Ovid, Metamorphoses (Brookes More translation, 1922), book 10

script.title: Pygmalion: The Sculptor Who Loved His Statue
script.description: A sculptor on the island of Cyprus carves a woman out of ivory, more beautiful than anyone alive, and falls in love with her. At the festival of the goddess of love, he makes a wish.

shorts.title: The Shipwrecked Sailor and the Serpent King
shorts.covers: A sailor is washed up on a magical island ruled by a giant golden serpent, who tells him a sad story and sends him home with treasure.
shorts.source: The Tale of the Shipwrecked Sailor, in W. M. Flinders Petrie, Egyptian Tales (1895)

script.title: The Shipwrecked Sailor and the Serpent King
script.description: A sailor is the only survivor of a storm and wakes on a magical island. Then the trees crack, the ground shakes, and a giant golden serpent comes looking for him.

shorts.title: Nergal and Ereshkigal: The God Who Married Death
shorts.covers: A god insults the queen of the dead, is summoned to her kingdom, and the story ends in a strange and stormy marriage.
shorts.source: Nergal and Ereshkigal, in R. W. Rogers, Cuneiform Parallels to the Old Testament (1912)

script.title: Nergal and Ereshkigal: Marrying Death
script.description: The queen of the dead cannot leave her dark kingdom, so the gods send her a share of their feast. One young god refuses to stand for her messenger, and she demands that he come down to her.

shorts.title: Branwen: The Insult That Started a War
shorts.covers: A Welsh princess married to the King of Ireland is mistreated, a starling carries her message home, and her giant brother wades across the sea.
shorts.source: The Mabinogion (Lady Charlotte Guest translation, 1849), Branwen the daughter of Llyr

script.title: Branwen: The Insult That Started a War
script.description: A Welsh princess is married to the King of Ireland, and then mistreated in his kitchen. She trains a starling to carry a letter across the sea to her giant brother.

shorts.title: Kaguya-hime: The Princess From the Moon
shorts.covers: A bamboo cutter finds a tiny girl glowing inside a stalk, she sets impossible tasks for her suitors, and the moon people come to take her back.
shorts.source: The Tale of the Bamboo Cutter, in F. Victor Dickins, Japanese Texts (1906)

shorts.title: Yu the Great: The Man Who Tamed the Flood
shorts.covers: After his father fails to hold back a world flood with stolen soil, Yu spends thirteen years digging channels and never goes home.
shorts.source: The Shujing (James Legge translation, 1865), the tribute of Yu, and E. T. C. Werner (1922)

shorts.title: The Sampo: The Magic Mill of Plenty
shorts.covers: A smith forges a mill that grinds out grain, salt and gold, and the heroes of Kalevala sail north to steal it back.
shorts.source: The Kalevala (John Martin Crawford translation, 1888), runos 10 and 39 to 43

shorts.title: Sedna: The Mother of the Sea
shorts.covers: A young woman is thrown from a boat by her father, her fingers become the seals and whales, and she rules the creatures from the sea floor.
shorts.source: Franz Boas, The Central Eskimo (1888), the tale of Sedna

shorts.title: Zal and the Simurgh: The Baby Raised by a Giant Bird
shorts.covers: A baby born with white hair is left on a mountain by his ashamed father, and is raised by the wise bird Simurgh.
shorts.source: Ferdowsi, The Shahnameh (A. G. and E. Warner translation, 1905), Zal

shorts.title: Melusine: The Wife Who Became a Serpent on Saturdays
shorts.covers: A knight marries a beautiful stranger who makes him swear never to see her on Saturdays, and he breaks his word.
shorts.source: Jean d'Arras, Melusine (A. K. Donald edition of the English version, 1895)

shorts.title: Thor and the Dwarf Who Talked Until Sunrise
shorts.covers: A dwarf arrives to marry Thor's daughter, and Thor quizzes him all night on the names of things until the sun turns him to stone.
shorts.source: The Poetic Edda (Henry Adams Bellows translation, 1923), Alvissmol

shorts.title: Thoth and the Five Extra Days
shorts.covers: Ra forbids the sky goddess Nut to give birth on any day of the year, so Thoth gambles with the moon and wins five new days.
shorts.source: Plutarch, On Isis and Osiris (Babbitt translation, Loeb 1936), chapter 12

shorts.title: Anzu: The Bird Who Stole the Tablet of Destinies
shorts.covers: A lion-headed bird steals the tablet that gives control of the universe, and the gods search for a champion brave enough to fight it.
shorts.source: The Myth of Anzu, in the Electronic Text Corpus of Sumerian Literature and Stephanie Dalley's notes

shorts.title: Blodeuwedd: The Woman Made of Flowers
shorts.covers: Magicians make a bride out of oak, broom and meadowsweet for a man cursed never to marry a human, and she plots his death.
shorts.source: The Mabinogion (Lady Charlotte Guest translation, 1849), Math the son of Mathonwy

shorts.title: Yuki-onna: The Woman of the Snow
shorts.covers: A woodcutter survives a blizzard when a pale spirit spares him on one condition, and years later he breaks his promise.
shorts.source: Lafcadio Hearn, Kwaidan (1904), Yuki-Onna

shorts.title: Jingwei: The Bird Who Tried to Fill the Sea
shorts.covers: A princess drowns in the eastern sea and is reborn as a small bird who carries pebbles and twigs to fill it, forever.
shorts.source: The Classic of Mountains and Seas (Shan Hai Jing), and E. T. C. Werner, Myths and Legends of China (1922)

shorts.title: Kullervo: The Tragic Son of Kalevala
shorts.covers: A boy sold as a slave suffers cruelty after cruelty, takes a terrible revenge, and learns a truth too heavy to live with.
shorts.source: The Kalevala (John Martin Crawford translation, 1888), runos 31 to 36

shorts.title: Raven Steals the Light
shorts.covers: The world is dark because a rich man keeps the sun, moon and stars in boxes, so Raven is reborn as his grandson to steal them.
shorts.source: John R. Swanton, Tlingit Myths and Texts (1909), the Raven cycle

shorts.title: Kaveh the Blacksmith: The Apron That Toppled a Tyrant
shorts.covers: A blacksmith whose sons were fed to the serpent king raises his leather apron on a spear and leads a revolt.
shorts.source: Ferdowsi, The Shahnameh (A. G. and E. Warner translation, 1905), Kaveh and Faridun

shorts.title: The Pied Piper of Hamelin
shorts.covers: A town refuses to pay the piper who rid it of rats, and he plays a new tune that leads away its children.
shorts.source: The Brothers Grimm, Deutsche Sagen (1816), the children of Hameln, and Robert Browning's poem (1842)

shorts.title: Savitri: The Wife Who Argued With Death
shorts.covers: A princess marries a man fated to die in a year, and when Yama comes for him she follows and outwits the god of death.
shorts.source: The Mahabharata (Kisari Mohan Ganguli translation), Vana Parva, the story of Savitri

shorts.title: The Doomed Prince
shorts.covers: A prince is told at birth he will die by a crocodile, a snake or a dog, and he sets out into the world to outrun his fate.
shorts.source: The Tale of the Doomed Prince, in W. M. Flinders Petrie, Egyptian Tales (1895)

shorts.title: Lugalbanda: Left Alone in the Mountains
shorts.covers: A young soldier falls ill on campaign and is abandoned in a cave, where he wins the favour of a giant bird and gains impossible speed.
shorts.source: Lugalbanda in the Mountain Cave, in the Electronic Text Corpus of Sumerian Literature (Oxford)

shorts.title: Taliesin: The Boy Who Tasted Three Drops
shorts.covers: A servant boy tastes a potion meant for someone else, flees a furious witch through many shapes, and is reborn as the greatest bard of Wales.
shorts.source: The Mabinogion (Lady Charlotte Guest translation, 1849), Taliesin

shorts.title: Hoichi the Earless
shorts.covers: A blind musician is summoned each night to play for a ghostly court, and a priest paints scripture on his body to hide him from the dead.
shorts.source: Lafcadio Hearn, Kwaidan (1904), the story of Mimi-Nashi-Hoichi

shorts.title: Madame White Snake
shorts.covers: A white snake spirit becomes a woman and marries a young man, until a monk sets out to expose her and imprison her under a pagoda.
shorts.source: The Legend of the White Snake, in E. T. C. Werner, Myths and Legends of China (1922)

shorts.title: Lemminkäinen's Mother: Raking the River of Death
shorts.covers: A reckless hero is killed and cut to pieces in the river of the underworld, and his mother rakes the water to put him back together.
shorts.source: The Kalevala (John Martin Crawford translation, 1888), runos 14 and 15

shorts.title: Sky Woman: The Fall That Made the Earth
shorts.covers: A woman falls from the sky world, birds catch her, and animals dive to bring up mud to build land on the back of a turtle.
shorts.source: J. N. B. Hewitt, Iroquoian Cosmology (1903)

shorts.title: Jamshid: The King Who Thought He Was a God
shorts.covers: A golden age king teaches people crafts and banishes illness, then claims divine credit and loses everything.
shorts.source: Ferdowsi, The Shahnameh (A. G. and E. Warner translation, 1905), Jamshid

shorts.title: Roland at Roncevaux: The Horn Blown Too Late
shorts.covers: Charlemagne's rear guard is ambushed in the Pyrenees, and the proud Roland refuses to blow his horn for help until it is too late.
shorts.source: The Song of Roland (C. K. Scott Moncrieff translation, 1919)

shorts.title: Nala and Damayanti: The King Who Gambled Away Everything
shorts.covers: A king possessed by a demon loses his kingdom at dice, abandons his wife in the forest, and both must find their way back.
shorts.source: The Mahabharata (Kisari Mohan Ganguli translation), Vana Parva, the story of Nala

shorts.title: The Two Brothers: Anpu and Bata
shorts.covers: A false accusation drives a younger brother into exile, where he hides his heart in a flower and is reborn again and again.
shorts.source: The Tale of Two Brothers, Papyrus d'Orbiney, in W. M. Flinders Petrie, Egyptian Tales (1895)

shorts.title: Enki and Ninhursag: The Curse of the Eight Plants
shorts.covers: The water god eats eight sacred plants in the paradise of Dilmun, the mother goddess curses him, and he falls deathly ill.
shorts.source: Enki and Ninhursag, in the Electronic Text Corpus of Sumerian Literature (Oxford)

shorts.title: Lugh and the Battle of Mag Tuired
shorts.covers: A young god of many skills is let into the court at Tara, and leads the gods of Ireland against the Fomorians and their one-eyed king.
shorts.source: Lady Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), the coming of Lugh and the great battle

shorts.title: Tamamo-no-Mae: The Nine-Tailed Fox at Court
shorts.covers: The most beautiful and learned woman at the emperor's court makes him fall ill, and a court astrologer reveals she is a fox spirit.
shorts.source: F. Hadland Davis, Myths and Legends of Japan (1912), the fox woman

shorts.title: The Butterfly Lovers
shorts.covers: A girl disguises herself as a boy to study, falls in love with a classmate, and when they cannot marry they become two butterflies.
shorts.source: The legend of Liang Shanbo and Zhu Yingtai, as retold in Chinese folklore collections

shorts.title: Eglė, Queen of Serpents
shorts.covers: A Lithuanian girl finds a grass snake in her clothes, must marry him, and discovers he is a prince of the sea.
shorts.source: The Lithuanian tale of Eglė the Queen of Serpents, as recorded in Baltic folklore collections

shorts.title: Coyote Steals Fire
shorts.covers: The people are cold and only the Fire Beings have flame, so Coyote plans a relay of animals to carry it away.
shorts.source: Katharine Berry Judson, Myths and Legends of the Pacific Northwest (1910)

shorts.title: Sinbad and the Island That Was a Whale
shorts.covers: On his first voyage Sinbad's crew lands on an island, lights a fire, and discovers they are standing on a sleeping whale.
shorts.source: The Thousand Nights and a Night (Richard Burton translation, 1885), the first voyage of Sindbad

shorts.title: The Death of Arthur and the Boat to Avalon
shorts.covers: Arthur fights his son Mordred at Camlann, orders Excalibur thrown back into the lake, and is carried away by three queens.
shorts.source: Thomas Malory, Le Morte d'Arthur (1485), book 21

shorts.title: Shakuntala and the Forgotten Ring
shorts.covers: A king marries a hermit's daughter in the forest and gives her his ring, a curse makes him forget her, and the lost ring is found in a fish.
shorts.source: Kalidasa, Shakuntala (Arthur W. Ryder translation, 1912), and the Mahabharata, Adi Parva
